interpretations.scope_one_line: Add a caching layer to the demo TokenService (TokenValidator) so repeated validations of the same token return a cached ValidationResult instead of re-running validation each call.
in_scope: Introduce a cache keyed on the token string (the request input) mapping to its ValidationResult
Check the cache at the top of TokenValidator.Validate and return the hit before re-running the length/empty checks
Populate the cache on a miss after computing the ValidationResult
Preserve the existing validation contract exactly: W0011 (empty), W0012 (too long), S0000 (valid) for the same inputs, cached or not
Handle the null-request / null-token edge so caching does not blow up on a null key (and ideally fix the pre-existing planted null-deref flaw rather than cache around a crash)
A bound or eviction policy so the cache cannot grow unbounded (size cap or simple LRU/expiry)
A unit test proving a second Validate call for the same token returns the same result and hits the cache, plus tests that the contract codes are unchanged
comparison_surfaces: TokenValidator.Validate method (the validation entry point being wrapped)
the new in-memory cache store (dictionary / MemoryCache abstraction)
cache key derivation from TokenRequest.Token
cache eviction / bounding policy
ValidationResult value type (what gets cached and returned)
unit-test surface for the service
key_behaviors: Same token validated twice returns an equivalent ValidationResult both times
First call computes and stores; second call serves from cache without recomputing
Returned codes for empty/too-long/valid inputs are identical whether served fresh or cached
Null or missing request/token does not crash and is not used as a poison cache key
Cache stays bounded so a stream of distinct tokens cannot exhaust memory
assumptions_i_had_to_make: The 'token service' means the demo deck/demo/sample-service/TokenValidator.cs (TokenService namespace) — the only token service in this repo; there is no real production token service here.
'Caching' means an in-process memory cache of validation results keyed by token, not a distributed/Redis cache (no infra is present and the demo is a single in-memory C# class).

Caching validation results is acceptable for this demo even though real token validation is often time-sensitive; no expiry/TTL was specified so a simple bounded cache (or short TTL) is the intended scope.
The result is deterministic for a given token in this demo (pure length checks), so caching is semantically safe.
This is a feature-implementation task on the demo service, NOT a request to modify the preflight framework's hooks/skills/lib; I should not treat it as a build-contract change.
Since the file carries a deliberately-planted null-deref flaw, correct caching also entails fixing that null guard rather than preserving the crash.

interpretations.scope_one_line: Add a result cache to the sample TokenService (TokenValidator.Validate) so repeated identical token-validation requests return a memoized ValidationResult instead of re-running the validation logic.
in_scope: Add an in-process cache keyed on the token string inside the TokenService namespace (deck/demo/sample-service/TokenValidator.cs)
Wrap TokenValidator.Validate so a previously-seen token returns the cached ValidationResult (W0011/W0012/S0000) without recomputing
Define cache semantics: what is the key (the token value), what is stored (the ValidationResult), and a bounded size / eviction or TTL so the cache can't grow unbounded
Preserve the existing validation contract exactly: empty token -> W0011, >4096 -> W0012, otherwise S0000
Handle the null/empty edge so caching does not change (or mask) the missing-input behavior
Add a unit test demonstrating a cache hit (same token twice) and that the returned result is unchanged from the uncached path
comparison_surfaces: service class / business logic (TokenValidator.Validate)
cache layer (new in-memory cache: dictionary or IMemoryCache, key=token, value=ValidationResult)
cache-key derivation (the token string itself)
cache eviction / sizing policy (max entries or TTL)
validation contract / result codes (W0011/W0012/S0000 must be preserved)
tests (unit test asserting cache hit + contract preservation)
key_behaviors: Identical repeated token inputs produce the same ValidationResult as the uncached path (caching must not change observable output)
First call computes and stores; subsequent calls for the same token read from cache (a hit, not a recompute)
The empty-token W0011 and >4096 W0012 paths still fire correctly whether served from cache or freshly computed
Cache is bounded (size cap or TTL) so it cannot grow without limit across distinct tokens
Caching the token string as a key is a knowingly accepted demo simplification (real secrets shouldn't be cached in plaintext) and is flagged, not silently shipped
assumptions_i_had_to_make: 'The token service' refers to the demo TokenService class in deck/demo/sample-service/TokenValidator.cs — the only token service in this repo; there is no production token-service codebase here
'Caching' means memoizing validation RESULTS keyed by the token input, not caching tokens issued to clients (this is a validator, not an issuer)
An in-process / in-memory cache is intended; no distributed cache (Redis/etc.) is implied by such a terse request
Validation is pure and deterministic for a given token, so a result cache is safe (no time/state dependence that would make a cached result wrong)
The existing planted null-check flaw in the demo is out of scope unless touching it is unavoidable — the task is adding caching, not fixing that demo flaw
No specific cache size, TTL, or eviction policy was given, so a sensible bounded default is chosen
This is a demo/sample artifact, so 'add caching' is a feature edit to that sample rather than a framework (hooks/skills/lib) change

interpretations.scope_one_line: Add token caching (cache the fetched/validated OAuth token so it isn't re-fetched on every call) to the demo .NET "TokenService", implementing it the way the framework's own rubric §M4.3 prescribes — IMemoryCache + single-flight — so it would pass preflight's own self-review.
in_scope: Add an IMemoryCache-backed token cache to the demo TokenService (deck/demo/sample-service/TokenValidator.cs / a TokenProvider) so the OAuth token is fetched once and reused until near expiry

Implement single-flight (SemaphoreSlim + double-checked lock) around the cache-miss fetch so concurrent callers don't all hit the token endpoint — directly avoiding the §M4.3 thundering-herd flaw the framework's own rubric flags
Set cache entry expiration shorter than the token's real TTL (e.g. AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow a few minutes under the 55-minute token lifetime) so a stale token is never served
Preserve the existing TokenValidator contract (W0011 empty / W0012 too-long / S0000 valid, plus the null-request guard) — caching is additive, not a behavior change
Run the change through the framework's self-review skill / Stage-1 rubric (the known-bad-token-cache fixture is the negative oracle: the new code must NOT trip §M4.3)
comparison_surfaces: cache layer (IMemoryCache / in-process token store)
data-access / downstream-client (the HttpClient call to the OAuth /oauth/token endpoint being cached)
concurrency-control (SemaphoreSlim single-flight / double-checked lock)
service-method API (GetTokenAsync / the TokenService public surface)
cache-expiration / invalidation policy (TTL vs token lifetime)
the framework's Stage-1 self-review rubric (§M4.3) as the verification surface
key_behaviors: First call fetches the token from the OAuth endpoint; subsequent calls within TTL return the cached token without a network round-trip
Under concurrent cache-miss, exactly one caller fetches and the rest await its result (single-flight) — no thundering herd on the token endpoint
Cached entry expires before the real token does, so an expired token is never returned to callers
On fetch failure the failed result is not poisoned into the cache (next call retries rather than serving a cached error)
Existing validation result codes and the null-input guard remain unchanged
assumptions_i_had_to_make: 'The token service' = the demo .NET service in deck/demo/sample-service (TokenService namespace) — this is framework-source repo, NOT a live production token service, so I'm reading it as the in-repo .NET artifact named TokenService rather than something to be cloned/migrated
'Caching' means caching the upstream OAuth token (avoid re-fetching), the same thing the known-bad-token-cache.cs fixture is about — not caching validation results or framework hook output

Single-flight is required, not optional: the framework's own §M4.3 rubric treats plain IMemoryCache.GetOrCreateAsync (no single-flight) as a major-severity finding, so a correct 'add caching' must include it
Use IMemoryCache (in-process) rather than a distributed cache (Redis) — the fixture and rubric reference IMemoryCache, and no multi-instance requirement was stated
The cache key is the token-type/endpoint (single 'oauth_token'-style key), since the demo service fetches one token, not per-user tokens
This is treated as a real code change to be self-reviewed through preflight, NOT as editing preflight's own hooks/lib engines

interpretations.scope_one_line: Add a result cache to the C# TokenService.TokenValidator so repeated Validate() calls for the same token return a memoized ValidationResult instead of recomputing.
in_scope: Add a cache (in-memory, keyed by the token string) inside or alongside TokenValidator in deck/demo/sample-service/TokenValidator.cs
On Validate(request): compute a cache key from request.Token, return the cached ValidationResult on hit, compute-and-store on miss
Preserve the existing validation logic exactly: empty -> W0011, length > 4096 -> W0012, otherwise S0000
A simple eviction/size bound or TTL so the cache cannot grow unbounded (concrete default chosen since unspecified)
Keep ValidationResult immutable so a cached instance is safe to hand back to multiple callers
Add/extend a unit test demonstrating a cache hit returns the same result without recomputation (matching the repo's xUnit-style fixtures)

cache layer (new in-memory keyed store, e.g. Dictionary/ConcurrentDictionary/MemoryCache)
cache key derivation (from request.Token)
eviction / size-bounding policy
thread-safety of the cache under concurrent callers
unit tests for the validator
key_behaviors: Same token validated twice yields the same ValidationResult and the second call hits the cache rather than re-running the length checks
Validation contract is unchanged: W0011 (empty), W0012 (>4096), S0000 (valid) still returned for the same inputs
Cache is bounded so a flood of distinct tokens cannot exhaust memory
Cache stores/keys on the token value; distinct tokens are independent entries
